classification.difficultyReason: Constructs and graphs a binomial distribution, interprets its shape and calculates a cumulative probability.

content.prompt: In a game, a person wins if a die comes up with the number 4 when rolled.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $X$ is the discrete random variable for getting a 4 when rolling a die 6 times, find all the possible values of $X$.

answer.worked: $X$ counts the number of 4s in six rolls, so $X\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5,6\}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw up a probability distribution table to show all the probabilities, as decimals, of getting a 4 when rolling the die 6 times. Give probabilities to 5 decimal places.

inlines.text: . Their decimal values are shown in the table.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw a bar graph to show this information.

answer.worked: Plot a separate bar at each integer $x=0,1,\ldots,6$, with height $P(X=x)$, using the unrounded probabilities.

spec.description: Seven narrow outlined bars, integer horizontal ticks 0–6, vertical ticks 0.1–0.5, arrowheads on both axes and no axis titles. Bar heights use exact probabilities, correcting the exaggerated source tail.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Describe the shape of the graph.

answer.worked: The graph is positively skewed: most probability is concentrated at small values, with a tail extending to the right.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the probability that a 4 will come up at least 3 times if the die is rolled 6 times. Give your answer to 5 decimal places.
